tools.name: doc_bates_multi
tools.description: Apply one consecutive Bates sequence to an ordered list of PDFs. Each file entry has input and output paths and an optional open or permissions password. The operation first validates every input/output and computes inclusive numeric intervals; dry_run returns that allocation without writing. Existing output files are never replaced. On application, files that cannot be edited or saved are reported individually and later files continue.

dry_run.description: Return each file's inclusive number interval without writing (default false).

output.description: New output PDF path; must not exist.

password.description: Open or permissions password, if needed.

prefix.description: Text before the number: at most 128 UTF-8 bytes, without # or >>.

suffix.description: Text after the number: at most 128 UTF-8 bytes, without # or >>.

tools.name: doc_batch
tools.description: Run convert, ocr and/or optimize over files and folders, one file at a time. recursive defaults to false. Preserve paths relative to each selected folder inside out_dir; duplicate inputs run once. Skip unsupported files, links and the output subtree. Existing outputs receive numbered names and are never replaced. Continue after per-file errors unless stop_on_error is true. Return completed/failed/skipped counts and per-file results. Discovery is bounded to 10000 entries and 64 folder levels. Convert must be first; each step can appear once. OCR uses installed models. Optimize uses Reduce File Size settings, optionally overriding target ppi (threshold 1.5 times ppi; black-and-white images go to the larger of ppi and 300) and JPEG quality; a larger candidate keeps the original bytes. Sources and open documents are unchanged.

tools.name: attachment_add
tools.description: Attach the file at path to the document (document level, the Attachments panel; not a paper-clip comment on a page). name defaults to the file's name; the attachment's key, unique in the document, is returned. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: attachment_delete
tools.description: Remove the document-level attachment with this name (as doc_info lists it). Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.description: Open a PDF file and return its document id, page count and whether it can be edited.

password.description: User or owner password for encrypted files.

tools.name: doc_list
tools.description: List the open documents with their ids, page counts and unsaved state.

tools.name: doc_info
tools.description: Metadata, page sizes and labels, bookmarks, annotations, form fields, links, layers, page transitions and display times, the destination it opens at, attachments, fonts, security and repair notes.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: doc_close
tools.description: Close a document. Fails if it has unsaved changes unless discard_changes is true.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: doc_save
tools.description: Save to its own file (an incremental update, which keeps signatures valid) or to a new path (a full rewrite). The write is atomic. flatten_fill_sign bakes Fill & Sign text, marks and signatures into the page first and removes those annotations; other comments and form fields stay. Omit it, or pass false, to leave them editable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

flatten_fill_sign.description: Bake Fill & Sign marks into the page before writing. Default false.

full.description: Force a full rewrite (or, with false, an incremental update).

path.description: Save as this file. Omit to save in place.

tools.name: doc_set_info
tools.description: Set a document information entry such as Title, Author, Subject or Keywords, or a custom property under any other name (no spaces, delimiters, / or #; at most 127 bytes; doc_info lists them under custom); an empty value removes it. When the file has XMP metadata, the matching XMP property (dc:title, dc:creator, dc:description, pdf:Keywords, xmp:CreatorTool, pdf:Producer) is changed too, so viewers that read XMP first show the new value. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_render
tools.description: Render one page to a PNG image (default 96 dpi, at most 600). When the picture is incomplete or approximate (content cut at the page's safety budget, a colour painted in a fallback colour), a JSON part follows the image: { page, warnings: [sentence, ...] }.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

hide_added_text.description: Render a retyping background without this added text item (added index from object_list). Mutually exclusive with hide_text_block. Does not modify the document.

hide_text_block.description: Render an inline editor background without this paragraph (number from text_paragraphs, resolved as text_edit does: refused once an edit merged that paragraph into a neighbour). Does not modify the document.

tools.name: model_render
tools.description: Draw a page's 3D model (a 3D annotation's PRC stream) to a PNG, framed to fill the image, with headlight shading on a white background. model is its 1-based position among the page's 3D models (default 1). direction is the view direction [x, y, z] from the eye towards the model (default [-1, 1, -1]); Z is up unless the view looks along Z. perspective defaults to true. U3D models can't be drawn yet and give an error. Does not modify the document.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: object_list
tools.description: List existing paragraphs, Image/Form artwork and added content once, with source kind/index references, displayed rectangles and document generation. Indexes change when content changes; use generation in object_move to reject stale references.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: object_move
tools.description: Atomically translate 1–1000 mixed references from object_list by [dx, dy] in displayed points (right/down). Preserves glyph codes, fonts, image data and relative spacing; success is one undo step. Text used as a clipping path and vertical text are refused. A bad/stale reference refuses the entire move.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

generation.description: Use generation returned by object_list to reject a stale selection.

tools.name: text_word_count
tools.description: Count Unicode words and characters on selected pages (default all), with totals and per-page counts. Table/code exclusions use PDF structure tags, not visual guesses; unclassified text is retained. Image exclusion removes Figure-tagged and invisible/OCR text. Does not run OCR. Copy permission is required. Fails rather than returning a partial total when a page cannot be read.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: text_extract
tools.description: Extract the text of some or all pages, in reading order. With rect, only the text inside that rectangle on each page, as Column select takes it: one row per visual line, side-by-side pieces (table cells) separated by a tab.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

rect.description: Column select: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in points from the top-left of the displayed page; a glyph counts when its centre is inside.

tools.name: text_find
tools.description: Find a phrase (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalised) and return matches in page order with page and line rectangles in points (origin top-left). Reads growing batches, looking one match past the limit for a continuation. Failed pages do not discard readable matches: warnings contains up to 100 {page, error, error_truncated} entries (errors capped at 1024 UTF-8 bytes), warning_count counts failed pages, and warnings_truncated reports a capped list. complete is false after a page failure or when more matches exist; next is present only for a match-limit continuation.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

limit.description: Maximum matches (default 500). When another match exists, next holds start_page and skip to continue. complete is false for either additional matches or failed pages; an exhausted search with warnings has no next.

skip.description: Matches to pass over on start_page before returning any (default 0).

tools.name: page_rotate
tools.description: Rotate pages by a multiple of 90 degrees (positive is clockwise): the listed pages (default all), filtered like Acrobat's Rotate Pages by subset (all, even, odd page numbers) and orientation (all, landscape, portrait). Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_enhance_camera
tools.description: Straighten a photographed document (Scan & OCR ▸ Enhance ▸ Camera image): the part of the page inside the four corners (x1, y1, … x4, y4 in top-left-origin points, any order, a convex quadrilateral; when omitted, the document's edges are found automatically, or an error says they could not be) is warped to an upright rectangle that replaces what the page shows, at the page picture's own resolution (at most 600 dpi). mode is how it looks: original, colour (default), greyscale or bw (black and white, stored losslessly). level (0–100, default 0) then cleans the photo up: even lighting so the paper turns white (casts, shadows, dark edges), more contrast, and from 60 no isolated specks; colour ink stays colour. For bw the level is the threshold (higher keeps fainter strokes black). The page's comments, links and bookmarks stay. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_delete
tools.description: Delete pages. Undoable until saved.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_move
tools.description: Move pages so the first of them lands at position `to` (1-based, counted before the move). Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_reverse
tools.description: Reverse the order of pages among the positions they occupy: the listed pages (at least two), or the whole document when pages is omitted. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_insert_blank
tools.description: Insert a blank page so it becomes page `at`. Size defaults to the neighbouring page. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_insert_file
tools.description: Insert pages of another PDF so the first becomes page `at`. Its bookmarks come along, collapsed under one bookmark named after the file, placed among the document's bookmarks where the pages went. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

pages.description: 1-based page numbers of the source file (default: all).

tools.name: page_extract
tools.description: Copy pages into a new PDF (links, bookmarks, fields and layers that belong to them come along). separate: true writes each page as its own file into out_dir; delete: true removes the pages from this document afterwards (undoable).

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

open.description: Also open the result as a new document (default: only when out is omitted).

out.description: File to write. Omit to open the result as a new unsaved document instead.

tools.name: doc_combine
tools.description: Combine files, in order, into one PDF (bookmarks are kept under one entry per file). Images (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, JPEG 2000) and .txt files are made into PDFs first. pages optionally chooses each file's pages, in step with paths: a range such as "1-3, 6" or null for all pages. passwords, also in step with paths, opens encrypted files (the open password, or the permissions password where a file's security doesn't allow copying pages; null for none). The result is not encrypted. Passwords are never echoed back. groups, also in step with paths, splits a file around others: entries with the same number (they must name the same path) are one file, copied once, so it keeps one bookmark at its first page, its links and its form fields; null for a file of its own. A group uses its first entry's password. When two files' forms name the same field, field_conflicts says what happens: "rename" (the default) keeps the fields separate by renaming the later one (Text1 becomes Text1-1) and the result lists renamed_fields as [[old, new], …] — scripts that refer to the old name are not rewritten; "merge" makes them one field, as before.

open.description: Also open the result as a new document (default: only when out is omitted).

out.description: File to write. Omit to open the result as a new unsaved document instead.

tools.name: doc_create_multiple
tools.description: Convert several files (PDFs, PNG/JPEG/JPEG 2000/TIFF/GIF/BMP images, .txt files) to PDF in one run. mode "combine" (default) joins them, in order, into one PDF with a bookmark per file; pages optionally chooses each file's pages, in step with paths (a range such as "1-3, 6" or null). mode "separate" writes one PDF per file into out_dir (files that are already PDFs are skipped; existing files are never overwritten) and reports each file's result.

open.description: Also open the result as a new document (default: only when out is omitted).

out.description: File to write. Omit to open the result as a new unsaved document instead.

tools.name: doc_split
tools.description: Split into several files written to out_dir: every N pages, before given pages, at top-level bookmarks (bookmarks: true; files named after them, repeated titles get -2, -3), or by file size (max_mb). Files are <name>-partK.pdf.

before.description: 1-based page numbers that start a new part.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: bookmark_list
tools.description: The bookmarks in outline order, one page at a time: each with its path (1-based, as the other bookmark tools take it), title, target page and open state, its colour ([r, g, b], 0-1) and bold or italic style when it has them, and its children on the same page. next is the offset of the following page, or null at the end. Bookmarks nested deeper than 33 levels are not listed.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

offset.description: Where the page starts, counted from 0 (the previous page's next)

tools.name: bookmark_add
tools.description: Add a bookmark that goes to a page, under a parent bookmark (or at the top level), at a position. It goes to the top of the page, or to a place on it: `top` and `left` are points from the top-left of the displayed page (like the destination bookmark_list reports), each optional, and a coordinate left out keeps the reader's position that way. The zoom is kept. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

left.description: Points from the left of the displayed page.

parent.description: Parent bookmark (omit for the top level): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

position.description: 1-based position among the parent's children (default: last).

top.description: Points from the top of the displayed page.

tools.name: bookmark_export
tools.description: The bookmark tree, or the subtree at path, as a list of nodes bookmark_import takes back unchanged. A node has title, page (1-based, null when it goes nowhere), open, and when set view ({type, values}: a destination type from ISO 32000-2 §12.3.2.2 Table 149 and its values in PDF user space, as the file stores them), color ([r, g, b], 0-1), bold, italic and children. truncated is true when bookmarks nested deeper than 33 levels were left out. With out, the tree is also written there as a JSON file {"bookmarks": [...]}, with "truncated": true when that is so; out is overwritten.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

out.description: A file path (relative to --root when set).

path.description: The bookmark whose subtree to export (omit for the whole outline): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

tools.name: bookmark_import
tools.description: Add a tree of bookmarks, as bookmark_export gives it (bookmarks) or as a JSON file it wrote (file), under a parent bookmark (or at the top level) at a position, or with replace in place of the whole outline. A bookmark whose page this document lacks is kept without a destination and listed in unmapped (1-based paths into the given tree). A view takes exactly its type's values (XYZ 3, FitR 4, FitH/FitV/FitBH/FitBV 1, Fit/FitB none). Give exactly one of bookmarks and file. A title may be empty but not missing; a key a node does not have is refused. Every node is checked before anything is written: at most 100000 bookmarks, nested at most 33 levels counting the parent's. truncated is true when the file says its export left bookmarks out. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

file.description: A file path (relative to --root when set).

parent.description: Parent bookmark (omit for the top level): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

position.description: 1-based position among the parent's children (default: last).

replace.description: Replace the document's bookmarks instead of adding to them (default false; leave parent out).

tools.name: bookmark_copy
tools.description: Copy the bookmarks of document from (or the subtree at path) into doc, by page number: under a parent bookmark (or at the top level) at a position, or with replace in place of doc's outline. A bookmark whose page doc lacks is kept without a destination and listed in unmapped (1-based paths into the copied tree). truncated is true when bookmarks nested deeper than 33 levels were left out of the copy. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

from.description: Id of the document to copy from.

parent.description: Parent bookmark in doc (omit for the top level): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

path.description: The bookmark whose subtree to copy (omit for the whole outline): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

position.description: 1-based position among the parent's children (default: last).

replace.description: Replace doc's bookmarks instead of adding to them (default false; leave parent out).

tools.name: bookmark_rename
tools.description: Change a bookmark's title. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

path.description: The bookmark: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

tools.name: bookmark_delete
tools.description: Delete a bookmark and the bookmarks under it. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

path.description: The bookmark: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

tools.name: bookmark_move
tools.description: Move a bookmark (with its children) under another parent, or within its level. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

parent.description: New parent (omit for the top level): 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

path.description: The bookmark to move: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

position.description: 1-based position among the new parent's children, counted after the bookmark is removed (default: last).

tools.name: bookmark_set_page
tools.description: Point a bookmark at another page. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

path.description: The bookmark: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

tools.name: bookmark_set_style
tools.description: Colour a bookmark's title and make it bold or italic (ISO 32000-2 §12.3.3: /C and /F), as bookmark_list reports them. Give any of color ([r, g, b], each 0-1; [0, 0, 0] is the default black), bold and italic; what is left out stays as it is. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

path.description: The bookmark: 1-based positions from the top level, e.g. [2, 1] = the first child of the second bookmark.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: text_styles
tools.description: The styles the document's text is set in, the largest first: font (without its subset tag), the size it is shown at in points, bold, italic, how many lines and pages use it, and the first line in it as a sample. For choosing the styles bookmark_from_text_styles makes bookmarks from (headings are usually the larger, rarer styles). Reads the first 5000 pages.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: bookmark_from_text_styles
tools.description: Make bookmarks from the lines set in chosen text styles, for documents whose headings are not tagged: levels lists one style per bookmark level ({font, size, bold, italic} as text_styles gives them; sizes within a quarter point match), the first level 1, the next nested under the bookmark before it, and so on. A heading set on several lines is one bookmark, and each goes to the top of its heading. They go under a new first bookmark titled "Untitled". Fails if no text is set in the styles. Returns the first page of the bookmark tree (see bookmark_list). Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: page_number
tools.description: Label a range of pages (e.g. i, ii, iii for front matter, or A-1, A-2 for an appendix). Later pages keep their labels. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

start.description: Number of the first page in the range (default 1).

style.description: Numbering style (default decimal; none = prefix only).

tools.name: form_fields
tools.description: Every interactive form field: name, type (text, checkbox, radio, combo, list, button, signature), value, options, page, rect (top-left-origin points) and rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counterclockwise), read-only and required flags. A calculated field includes calculate: {op, fields} or {notation} as form_set_props takes them, or {script} for a custom Calculate script (set with form_set_script). Push buttons include caption (first widget's normal label) and captions [{widget, caption}] for all widgets (1-based).

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_fill
tools.description: Set several fields at once (one undo step). values maps field names (from form_fields) to: a string for text fields, combo boxes and radio groups (an option), true/false for check boxes, an array of strings for multi-select lists. Appearances are regenerated so every viewer shows the values. A value whose characters the field's font can't draw (Chinese in a Helvetica field) is still saved; `warnings` in the result names the field and character: PdfCraft draws `?` there and asks other viewers to redraw the field from its value.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_reset
tools.description: Reset fields to their default values: all of them, or only those listed. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_add_field
tools.description: Add a form field on a page. type: text, date, checkbox, radio, combo, list, button, image (a picture placeholder; fill it with form_set_image), signature. rect in points from the top-left of the displayed page [x0, y0, x1, y1]. name defaults to Acrobat's next free name (Text1, Check Box1, Group1, Dropdown1, List Box1, Button1, Image1, Signature1, Date1); a dotted name such as MASTER.first makes the field first under the parent field MASTER. Radio buttons join the radio group named by group (a new group otherwise) with the export value export. Returns the field's name. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_add_field_table
tools.description: Divide rect into rows and columns of text fields, one per cell, as one undo step. rect in points from the top-left of the displayed page [x0, y0, x1, y1]; rows 1-100 from the top; columns 1-50, or as many as names or widths list. Each column names its cells from its pattern in names: an N on its own after _ - / or : (price_N), # or {row} is the row number, {col} the column number, {seq} counts every cell along the rows, starting at first_row; with none of them the row number goes at the end. Rows count from first_row (default 1). Without names the columns are Table1_N, Table1_c2_N, … using the first free TableK. widths are relative (default equal); row_gap and column_gap are points between cells (default 0). Nothing is added if a cell would be under 4 points or a name would contain a period, repeat, or already exist; the error says which. Returns the fields' names. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

widths.description: Relative column widths, one per column.

annotations.title: Prepare form: add a table of text fields

tools.name: stamp_custom
tools.description: Stamp a picture: a PDF page (file_page, default 1, kept as vector content in a form XObject) or an image file. Either centred at at [x, y] (points from the top-left of the displayed page) at its natural size, at most 200 pt, or fitted inside rect [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the same coordinates; each side 1–14400 pt), scaled to keep its shape and centred in the box. Like at, rect is not clipped to the page. Pass at or rect, not both. name labels it (default: the file name). Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: model_add
tools.description: Add a 3D model (Acrobat: Rich Media ▸ Add 3D): the U3D or PRC file at path, recognised by its first bytes, as a 3D annotation in rect [x0, y0, x1, y1] (points from the top-left of the displayed page; each side 1–14400 pt; at most 256 MiB). Its poster, what prints and what readers show until the model is activated, is the picture at poster (a PDF page, poster_page default 1, or an image) fitted inside rect keeping its shape and centred; without poster, a frame labelled "3D model". activation: click (default), page_open or page_visible. name is its description (default: the file name). No views are added: readers open the model on its own default view. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_set_image
tools.description: Show an image file (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF or BMP) in an image field or button, scaled to fit and centred (what clicking an image field does). On an XFA form the picture is kept in its data too (base64, as Designer saves it) and the form shows it from there. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_set_props
tools.description: Change field properties: give field for one field, or fields for a list of unique field names (1–1000). A bulk change is atomic and one Undo step; an invalid or locked field leaves every field unchanged. Only the given properties change, and partial appearance changes preserve each field's other colours and font. name (rename: a dotted name such as MASTER.first is the full name and moves the field under those parent fields; a plain name renames it within its parent), rect (position), rotation and caption require a single field. A rename also renames the field in the calculations that read it (calculate field lists and notation, and getField calls naming it in a string literal; names built at run time are not rewritten), in the same Undo step, and formulas_updated lists the fields whose calculation changed. caption changes one push-button normal label (widget: 1-based index, default 1); an empty string clears it. Other widgets and icon-only layouts are preserved. General and Options: tooltip, read_only, required, multiline, max_length (0 = no limit), options (combo/list items), font_size (0 = auto), format, validate, calculate (Acrobat's native AF rules). Options: align (left, center, right), default (Reset form's value; check boxes/radio buttons use their on state, "" for off), flags { scroll, rich_text, password, file_select, spell_check, comb (needs max_length), sort, editable, multi_select, commit_immediately }, check_style (check boxes/radio buttons: check, circle, cross, diamond, square, star). rotation is 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counterclockwise and swaps width/height when the axis changes. Undoable.

appearance.description: Appearance tab: border, fill, text_color (#RRGGBB, a name or "none"), width (0–12 points; 1 thin, 2 medium, 3 thick), style (solid, dashed, beveled, inset, underline), font (helvetica, times, courier).

calculate.description: Calculate tab: {"op": "sum"|"product"|"average"|"min"|"max", "fields": ["a", "b"]}, {"notation": "Price * Qty"} (simplified field notation), or "none".

caption.description: Normal push-button label; an empty string clears it. Requires a single field.

check_style.description: Check boxes and radio buttons: the mark shown when on.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

export_value.description: Checkbox/radio export value; preserves appearance states and selection. Requires a single field.

fields.description: Apply the same changes to these fields in one atomic edit. Use either field or fields.

locked.description: Lock the field's properties (only unlocking is accepted while locked).

rect.description: Move/resize: points from the top-left of the displayed page.

rotation.description: Widget rotation in degrees, counterclockwise. Changing between horizontal and vertical swaps the rectangle around its center.

validate.description: Validate tab: {"min": 0, "max": 100} (either may be left out, or null) or "none".

widget.description: Widget whose caption or export value changes (1-based, default 1). Requires caption or export_value. See form_fields.captions and export_values.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: doc_remove_marks
tools.description: Remove every header and footer, watermark or background PdfCraft (or a compatible tool) added. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

annotations.title: Remove header & footer, watermark or background

tools.name: doc_export_images
tools.description: Write pages as PNG, JPEG or TIFF files (`<name>_page_<n>.png|jpg|tif`) into a folder, at a resolution (default 150 dpi). JPEG and TIFF are flattened onto white paper. doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: accessibility_autotag_preview
tools.description: Propose paragraph and heading tags for visible text blocks on one page. Returns page bounds, tentative roles and reasons. Does not change the PDF or claim accessibility compliance. Images, tables, lists, annotations and existing structure require separate review.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: accessibility_autotag_form_fields
tools.description: Write `/Form` tags, widget structure-parent keys, and a parent tree for all page widgets in an untagged AcroForm. Existing tag trees are refused for review. Text, figures, links, and other content are not tagged.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

pages.description: 1-based page numbers for the page rules (default: all).

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

after.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

all.description: Include rules that are off by default (colour contrast).

before.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.description: Apply the checker's automatic fix for a rule: primary-language (value: the language, e.g. en-US), title (value: the title; default the current title or file name; also shows it in the title bar) or tab-order (every page tabs in structure order). doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: accessibility_figures

tools.name: accessibility_set_alt
tools.description: Set a figure's alternate text (alt; empty or omitted clears it), or mark it decorative (decorative: true: its content becomes an artifact and the figure leaves the tags). figure is a number from accessibility_figures. Returns the figures. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: accessibility_tags
tools.description: List reachable indirect structure tags in document order with PDF object number, generation, nearest indirect parent, depth, page, type, title, actual text, alternate text, language, a table's summary and a header cell's scope, one page at a time: count is how many tags match, next the offset of the following page (null at the end). types, pages and max_depth keep only some tags. doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.description: List the marked-content references directly owned by one reachable indirect structure tag, including page, MCID and extracted text.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: accessibility_set_tag_property
tools.description: Set or clear one property of a reachable indirect structure tag. Use object and generation from accessibility_tags. Properties: type, title, actual_text, alternate_text, language, summary (Table tags: the table's Summary attribute), scope (TH tags: Row, Column or Both). Summary and scope are written in the tag's Table attribute object (/A, /O /Table); the role map decides a tag's type. Empty or omitted value clears text properties, summary and scope; type requires a nonempty PDF name. Undoable.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: form_merge_data
tools.description: Collect the field values of form data files (FDF, XFDF) or filled-in PDF forms into one CSV file at path: a column per field name, a row per file. Returns the row and column counts.

tools.name: js_run

Field changes and resetForm are applied as one undoable step; returns the script's alerts (each with its message, title, icon and buttons, in order; every question is still answered OK), console output, requests (print, page, url, submit), error, and the errors of document-level scripts that failed (the rest still ran).

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

doc.description: Document id from doc_open or doc_list.

tools.name: doc_export_office

HTML uses rich styling by default; set html_mode to simple for CSS-free headings, paragraphs, emphasis and tables. Simple HTML keeps text and inline images but omits colour and layout styling. Word uses borderless inferred tables and positioned editable shapes on pages with artwork, rotated or large text; each source page retains its size. Font matching and vector graphics remain limited. Export reads forms 50 deep and up to 50 000 a page, counting forms the page draws itself. Pages that go past either limit, or that have pictures past what one export may hold or decode, are listed in truncated_pages, with a warning; what was left out is missing.

color.description: #RRGGBB or a name: yellow, red, orange, green, blue, purple, pink, black, gray, white.

tools.name: image_edit
tools.description: Change one of a page's images (number from page_images): action move (rect: new full placement box in top-left-origin points, based on page_images.rect), crop (rect: the part to keep, top-left-origin points; the pixels stay in place and page_images.visible_rect shows the result; a later move carries the crop along), remove_crop (remove a crop created by PdfCraft while preserving clipping paths from the original document), rotate (quarters clockwise, default 1), rotate_by (degrees: any angle clockwise about the visible centre; the box in page_images then becomes the turned image's bounding box), transform (matrix: 6 numbers [a, b, c, d, e, f] in top-left-origin points, applied after the current placement so a point (x, y) of the image moves to (a·x + c·y + e, b·x + d·y + f); finite, with a·d − b·c not 0; the box in page_images becomes the transformed image's bounding box), flip_horizontal (reflect left/right on the displayed page), flip_vertical (reflect top/bottom on the displayed page; both flip actions follow the page rotation), replace (path: an image file, drawn in the same place), delete, or arrange: bring_to_front, send_to_back, bring_forward, send_backward (reorder stacking order among content on the page; errors when the image is already at the requested limit; arranging an added image converts it into an ordinary page image). Undoable. The selected image crop transforms with its pixels, isolating shared path scopes while retaining neighboring painting. Text-outline clips return a clear error. Rotation/flip use the visible centre. Form artwork supports move/resize/rotate/flip/delete as a group; replace and image_save only support raster images.

tools.name: text_edit
tools.description: Replace the text of one paragraph (paragraph, from text_paragraphs: rewrapped to the paragraph's width with its line spacing) or one line (line, from text_lines) in place, keeping position, size and colour. For a mixed-style region, editor_text supplies visual row breaks; surviving text keeps its source-run styles and inserted text inherits the surrounding run. For a paragraph, also change its formatting: font (helvetica, times, courier) with bold/italic, size (points), color (#rrggbb), align (left, center, right, justify), underline, line_spacing (× size), char_spacing (points) and scale (horizontal, percent), or move it (dx, dy in points; up is +dy) and rewrap it to a new width (points); text may then be omitted. Its own font is reused when it can show every character and no font/weight change is requested; otherwise it uses a standard font matching the source style or, for text no standard font can show, real fallback outlines from PdfCraft's own faces, from the one that has every character: the craft-fonts Japanese faces (Mincho/Gothic matching the requested/source family and available weight) or, behind them, the bundled Inter face, which carries the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters they lack (Uzbek қ, Kazakh ә). The result shows the font used, and for a paragraph its text unless the document's security doesn't allow copying. Missing Japanese weights use Regular, not synthetic bold; the small web build has only Gothic Regular. Paragraph bold may be set without font to keep the source family. Text that no available font can show is refused. A paragraph number is refused when an earlier edit merged that paragraph into a neighbour (list the page again); the result's stale_paragraphs names the numbers gone. Undoable.

tools.name: text_script
tools.description: Format text ▸ Superscript or Subscript on one paragraph (paragraph, from text_paragraphs), or on range [start, end): UTF-8 byte offsets of its editor_text. The characters take the Unicode superscript or subscript forms (2 → ², 2 → ₂; the font must have those glyphs, and extracted text contains them); text already in that script goes back to plain characters. Characters Unicode has no such form for (q, a space) stay unchanged and do not determine the selection's script state. Mixed plain and target-script characters normalize to that script, then to plain text on the next call (H₂2 → H₂₂ → H22); a second toggle does not reconstruct the original mixture. Use Undo to restore the exact prior text. The paragraph is then rewritten as text_edit rewrites it, with the same result fields. Refused when no character would change. Undoable. Mathematical minus U+2212 has its own script mapping; ASCII hyphen-minus stays unchanged.

tools.description: Write an optimized copy to `path` (Acrobat's PDF Optimizer). preset: standard (default; Reduce File Size's choices) or mobile (images to 96 ppi above 144, JPEG high quality); the options below change it. compatibility: retain (default; keeps the document's version, or 1.5 when object streams are written), 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7 or 2.0. merge_fragments (default true) first puts a page picture drawn as many stacked image strips (as some PDF printers write it) back together into one image, so it can be resampled (merged_images, fragments_merged). color / gray: { downsample, ppi, above_ppi, compression: jpeg|zip|retain, quality 1–100 } (defaults: downsample to 150 ppi above 225, JPEG 60). mono: { downsample, ppi, above_ppi, compression: ccitt_g4|jbig2|retain } for black-and-white images and image masks (default: averaged down to 300 ppi above 450 ppi, counted in images_resampled; stored losslessly as CCITT Group 4 or JBIG2 (or 1-bit Flate, once resampled or packed from more bits) when that is smaller, up to 16 JBIG2 images sharing one symbol dictionary (/JBIG2Globals) where that is smaller still (image masks and DeviceGray images named directly, of at most 64 Mi pixels, which redaction can store again without it), Group 3 fax images, JBIG2 images, black-and-white RGB and indexed images using only palette entries 0 and 1 among them, counted in images_recompressed; retain resamples only, a CCITT image staying CCITT, a JBIG2 image JBIG2 and any other becoming Flate). Images past what one run may decode stay as they are, counted in images_refused; streams it only stores with Flate past that stay LZW, uncounted. Images are measured where pages draw them and replaced only when smaller. discard_*: thumbnails (default true), alternate_images (true), tags, print_settings; flate_unencoded (true); object_streams (default true; always off for 1.4); lzw_to_flate (true) decodes LZW streams and stores them with Flate instead, leaving any it cannot decode unchanged (lzw_streams counts the streams converted); remove_invalid_links and remove_unreferenced_dests (true); images and forms the pages list but never draw are always dropped (unused_xobjects). discard: Remove Hidden Information categories (metadata, attachments, comments, form-fields, hidden-text, hidden-layers, bookmarks, links-actions-scripts, private-data). Signed documents are refused. The open document is unchanged.

instructions: PdfCraft makes and edits PDFs. To make a new PDF, write the content as Markdown and call pdf_create: it lays the document out properly and gives the user the file to download. Never write Python or other code to generate a PDF. To give the user any file a tool wrote (doc_save, doc_export_office, ...), call file_attach with its path. Open a file with doc_open to get a document id, then inspect (doc_info, text_extract, text_find, page_render) or edit it (page_*, doc_set_info). Edits are undoable (edit_undo) and stay in memory until doc_save. Page numbers are 1-based. Open documents are also resources: pdfcraft://doc/{doc}/info, /text, /page/{page}/text and /page/{page}/image. command_list discovers command ids and tool schemas; command_run executes one, command_batch runs several. doc_inspect returns open document state; render_preview returns a bounded PNG.
